body.text: The Root Fossil revives into Lileep, which evolves into Cradily at level 40.

sections.heading: Playthrough Notes
body: Slow defensive Pokémon with recovery and chip-damage potential.
Cradily is difficult to knock out and can heal itself, but it defeats route trainers more slowly than most fossil choices. Can be a clutch wall in Gym Battles/Elite Four.
Use recovery and status or draining moves to outlast opponents. Cradily is better at staying power than quick knockouts.
Reliable but slow; choose it for survivability rather than speed.

sections.heading: Strengths and Weaknesses
body: Strengths: Good mixed bulk. Useful Grass coverage against Water and Ground Pokémon. Can use recovery moves in many games. Few opponents can knock it out in one hit without exploiting a weakness.
Weaknesses: Very slow. Only moderate offensive power. Weak to Fighting, Bug, Ice, and Steel. Can make routine trainer battles take longer.

sections.heading: Choice Context

body.text: Choose the Root Fossil for durability and recovery. Choose the Claw Fossil for faster, more direct physical offense.

body: Claw Fossil is more straightforward for a normal playthrough, but Root Fossil can be more useful if the team needs a defensive wall or recovery.
